subject: chem
title: Classification of Elements & Periodicity
syllabus: Modern periodic law and present form of the periodic table, s, p, d and f block elements, periodic trends in properties of elements atomic and ionic radii, ionization enthalpy, electron gain enthalpy, valence, oxidation states, and chemical reactivity.

body: Modern periodic law: properties are periodic functions of ATOMIC NUMBER (Mendeleev used atomic mass).
Period = principal quantum number of the outer shell; a period holds 2 × (number of orbitals being filled) elements: 2, 8, 8, 18, 18, 32, 32.
Blocks by last subshell: s (groups 1–2), p (13–18), d (3–12), f (lanthanoids/actinoids placed below).
Elements beyond 100: digit roots nil 0, un 1, bi 2, tri 3, quad 4, pent 5, hex 6, sept 7, oct 8, enn 9 + "-ium" (111 = Unununium).
Across a period: radius falls (more Z_{eff}). Down a group: rises (new shells).
Exceptions to remember: Ga (135 pm) < Al (143 pm) — 3d electrons shield poorly; the As → Bi steps are small for the same reason.
Cations are smaller than their atoms, anions larger. Isoelectronic species: more protons → smaller (N^{3−} > O^{2−} > F^{−} > Na^{+} > Mg^{2+} > Al^{3+}).
Noble-gas radii are van der Waals radii — not comparable with covalent ones.
Energy to remove the outermost electron from an isolated gaseous atom — always endothermic; IE_{2} > IE_{1}.
Rises across a period, falls down a group. Kinks: Be > B (2s full vs 2p^{1}), N > O (half-filled 2p); Mg > Al, P > S.
Group 13: B ≫ Tl > Ga > Al > In. Group 14: C > Si > Ge > Pb > Sn.
A huge jump between IE_{n} and IE_{n+1} means the core has been reached (Na: 496 → 4562).
Δ_{eg}H: usually negative for halogens; positive for noble gases (and N, Be, Mg) — adding the electron is uphill.
Most negative: Cl (−349) > F (−328) > Br (−325) > I. O (−141) is less negative than S (−200): small, crowded 2p.
Electronegativity (Pauling): F 4.0 > O 3.5 > N = Cl 3.0 > Br 2.8 > C = S = I 2.5. Rises across, falls down.
Metallic character ~ low IE/EN: increases down and to the left. Oxides: left basic, right acidic, middle amphoteric (Al_{2}O_{3}).

check.why: F is too small and crowded.

formulas: nil un bi tri quad pent hex sept oct enn + ium
traps: Ga is smaller than Al; Tl has higher IE₁ than In.
Cl, not F, has the most negative electron gain enthalpy.
B has lower IE₁ than Be; O lower than N.
Anions are bigger than their atoms — "ions are always smaller" is false.
Mg is more metallic than Al (K > Mg > Al > B).
Period n holds 2 × (orbitals being filled), not n² elements.

pyq.q: The elements of Group 13 with highest and lowest first ionisation enthalpies are respectively :
sol: Highest B, lowest In (poor d/f shielding raises Ga and Tl).

pyq.q: The incorrect relationship in the following pairs in relation to ionisation enthalpies is :
sol: Removing an electron from Mn^{2+} (stable d^{5}) costs 3248 kJ; from Fe^{2+} (d^{6} → d^{5}) only 2957 kJ → Mn^{2+} > Fe^{2+}, so (1) is wrong.
Mn^{+} (d^{5}s^{1}) < Cr^{+} (d^{5}, half-filled); higher charge always raises IE.

pyq.q: The correct order of the first ionization enthalpy is
sol: Tl 589 > Ga 579 > Al 577 (B 801 is highest of all, so (3) fails at Al > Ga).

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I : The correct order of first ionization enthalpy values of Li, Na, F and Cl is Na < Li < Cl < F. Statement II : The correct order of negative electron gain enthalpy values of Li, Na, F and Cl is Na < Li < F < Cl. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: −Δ_{eg}H: Na 53 < Li 60 < F 328 < Cl 349 ✓ (F is small and crowded, so Cl gains an electron more readily).
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

pyq.q: The correct order of first ionization enthalpy values of the following elements is : (A) O (B) N (C) Be (D) F (E) B. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: Be > B (2s full) and N > O (2p half-full) are the two famous kinks.

pyq.q: What is the energy (in J atom^{−1}) required for the following process? Li^{2+}(g) → Li^{3+}(g) + e^{−} (Take the ionization energy for the H atom in the ground state as 2.18 × 10^{−18} J atom^{−1})
sol: Li^{2+} is hydrogen-like (one electron, Z = 3): IE = 2.18 × 10^{−18} × Z^{2}.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The second ionization enthalpy of B, Al and Ga is in the order of B > Al > Ga. Statement II : The correct order in terms of first ionization enthalpy is Si < Ge < Pb < Sn. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: IE_{2}: B 2427, Al 1817, Ga 1979 → Ga > Al, so I is false.
IE_{1}: Si 786 > Ge 762 > Pb 716 > Sn 709 — II reverses it → false.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement (I): The first ionization energy of Pb is greater than that of Sn. Statement (II): The first ionization energy of Ge is greater than that of Si. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sol: Pb 716 > Sn 709 (poorly shielding 4f electrons) → I true.
Ge 762 < Si 786 → II false.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: The element having the highest first ionization enthalpy is
sol: N 1402 > C 1086 > Si 786 > Al 577 (small, half-filled 2p).

pyq.q: First ionisation enthalpy values of first four group 15 elements are given below. Choose the correct value for the element that is a main component of apatite family :
sol: Apatite Ca_{10}(PO_{4})_{6}X_{2} is a phosphorus mineral; IE_{1}(P) = 1012 kJ mol^{−1} (N 1402, As 947, Sb 834).

pyq.q: The 1^{st} ionization enthalpy for Mg is +737 kJ/mol. The most probable estimated value of the 2^{nd} ionization enthalpy of Mg is ____ .
sol: Removing the second 3s electron from a positive ion costs about twice as much: IE_{2} ≈ 1450 kJ mol^{−1} (still the same shell, so not a huge jump).

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement I: The first ionization enthalpy of Cr is lower than that of Mn. Statement II: The second and third ionization enthalpies of Cr are higher than those of Mn. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: IE_{1}: Cr 653 < Mn 717 → I true.
o: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement I : C < O < N < F is the correct order in terms of first ionization enthalpy values. Statement II: S > Se > Te > Po > O is the correct order in terms of the magnitude of electron gain enthalpy values. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: |Δ_{eg}H|: S 200 > Se 195 > Te 190 > Po 174 > O 141 ✓ (small O repels the incoming electron).
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

pyq.q: The correct trend in the first ionization enthalpies of the elements in the 3^{rd} period of periodic table is :
sol: Al 577 < Si 786 < S 1000 < P 1012 < Cl 1251 (P > S: half-filled 3p).

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The second ionisation enthalpy of Na is larger than the corresponding ionisation enthalpy of Mg. Statement II: The ionic radius of O^{2−} is larger than that of F^{−}. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
sol: IE_{2}(Na) breaks into the neon core: 4562 ≫ IE_{2}(Mg) 1450 → I true.
Isoelectronic: O^{2−} (Z = 8) 140 pm > F^{−} (Z = 9) 133 pm → II true.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

pyq.q: First and second ionization enthalpies of lithium are 520 kJ mol^{−1} and 7297 kJ mol^{−1} respectively. Energy required to convert 3.5 mg lithium (g) into Li^{2+}(g) [Li(g) → Li^{2+}(g)] is ____ kJ. (nearest integer) [Molar mass of Li = 7 g mol^{−1}]
In a period, the first ionisation enthalpy of the element at extreme left and the negative electron gain enthalpy of the extreme right element, except noble gases, are respectively.
sol: Alkali metal at the left: lowest IE. Halogen at the right: most negative Δ_{eg}H (highest −Δ_{eg}H).

pyq.q: The correct order of first (Δ_{i}H_{1}) and second (Δ_{i}H_{2}) ionisation enthalpy values of Cr and Mn are : A. Δ_{i}H_{1}: Cr > Mn B. Δ_{i}H_{2}: Cr > Mn C. Δ_{i}H_{1}: Mn > Cr D. Δ_{i}H_{2}: Mn > Cr. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: IE_{1}: Mn 717 > Cr 653 (C). IE_{2}: Cr 1592 > Mn 1509 (B) — Cr^{+} is the stable d^{5}.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement (I): The first ionisation enthalpy of group 14 elements is higher than the corresponding elements of group 13. Statement (II) : Melting points and boiling points of group 13 elements are in general much higher than those of corresponding elements of group 14. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
sol: Group 14 (C, Si: giant covalent) melt far higher than group 13 → II incorrect.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

pyq.q: The property/properties that show irregularity in first four elements of group-17 is/are : (A) Covalent radius (B) Electron affinity (C) Ionic radius (D) First ionization energy. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: Radii and IE change steadily down the group.
Electron affinity is irregular: Cl (349) > F (328) > Br > I.

pyq.q: Electronic configuration of four elements A, B, C and D are given below : (A) 1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{3} (B) 1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{4} (C) 1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{5} (D) 1s^{2}2s^{2}2p^{2}. Which of the following is the correct order of increasing electronegativity (Pauling's scale) ?
sol: A = N, B = O, C = F, D = C.

pyq.q: Which of the following statements are correct? A. The process of adding an electron to a neutral gaseous atom is always exothermic. B. The process of removing an electron from an isolated gaseous atom is always endothermic. C. The 1^{st} ionization energy of boron is less than that of beryllium. D. The electronegativity of C is 2.5 in CH_{4} and CCl_{4}. E. Li is the most electropositive among elements of group I. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sol: A ✗ (noble gases: Δ_{eg}H > 0). B ✓. C ✓ (B 801 < Be 899).
D ✗ (EN depends on the atoms attached / hybridisation). E ✗ (Cs is the most electropositive).

pyq.q: Which of the following electronegativity order is incorrect?
sol: Mg 1.2 < Al 1.5, so "Al < Mg" is wrong.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Fluorine has most negative electron gain enthalpy in its group. Statement II: Oxygen has least negative electron gain enthalpy in its group. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate from the options given below.
sol: Cl (−349) is more negative than F (−328) → I false.
O (−141) is the least negative in group 16 → II true.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: The correct sequence of electron gain enthalpy of the elements listed below is A. Ar B. Br C. F D. S. Choose the most appropriate from the options given below:
sol: As signed values: Ar > S > Br > F → A > D > B > C.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement I: Elements 'X' and 'Y' are the most and least electronegative elements, respectively among N, As, Sb and P. The nature of the oxides X_{2}O_{3} and Y_{2}O_{3} is acidic and amphoteric, respectively. Statement II : BCl_{3} is covalent in nature and gets hydrolysed in water. It produces [B(OH)_{4}]^{−} and [B(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{3+} in aqueous medium. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: X = N (N_{2}O_{3} acidic), Y = Sb (Sb_{2}O_{3} amphoteric) → I true.
Boron has no d orbitals (max covalency 4), so [B(H_{2}O)_{6}]^{3+} cannot form; BCl_{3} gives B(OH)_{3} + HCl → II false.
o: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The correct order of electronegativity of fluorine, oxygen and nitrogen is F > O > N. Statement II: The oxidation state of oxygen in OF_{2} is +2 and in Na_{2}O is −2. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
sol: EN: F 4.0 > O 3.5 > N 3.0 ✓. In OF_{2}, F is more electronegative → O is +2; in Na_{2}O, O is −2 ✓.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: Elements X and Y belong to Group 15. The difference between the electronegativity values of 'X' and phosphorus is higher than that of the difference between phosphorus and 'Y'. 'X' & 'Y' are respectively
In case of isoelectronic species the size of F^{−}, Ne and Na^{+} is affected by:
sol: Same electrons (10), same shells — only the nuclear charge differs: Z = 9, 10, 11 pulls harder → F^{−} > Ne > Na^{+}.
o: None of the factors because their size is the same
Electron-electron interaction in the outer orbitals

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement (I) : The metallic radius of Al is less than that of Ga. Statement (II) : The ionic radius of Al^{3+} is less than that of Ga^{3+}. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
sol: Metallic radius: Al 143 pm > Ga 135 pm (poor shielding by 3d) → I incorrect.
Ionic: Al^{3+} 53.5 < Ga^{3+} 62 pm → II correct.
o: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

pyq.q: The correct orders among the following are A. Atomic radius : B < Al < Ga < In < Tl B. Electronegativity: Al < Ga < In < Tl < B C. Density: Tl < In < Ga < Al < B D. 1st Ionisation Energy : In < Al < Ga < Tl < B. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
sol: C ✗ (density rises down the group: B 2.35 … Tl 11.85). D ✓ (558 < 577 < 579 < 589 < 801).

pyq.q: Given below are the pairs of group 13 elements showing their relation in terms of atomic radius. (B < Al), (Al < Ga), (Ga < In) and (In < Tl). Identify the elements present in the incorrect pair and in that pair find out the element (X) that has higher ionic radius (M^{3+}) than the other one. The atomic number of the element (X) is
sol: Wrong pair: Al < Ga (actually Al 143 > Ga 135).

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement I : The metallic radius of Na is 1.86 Å and the ionic radius of Na^{+} is lesser than 1.86 Å. Statement II : Ions are always smaller in size than the corresponding elements. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: Anions are LARGER than their atoms (Cl^{−} 184 > Cl 99) → II false.
o: Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true

pyq.q: The statement(s) that are correct about the species O^{2−}, F^{−}, Na^{+} and Mg^{2+}. (A) All are isoelectronic (B) All have the same nuclear charge (C) O^{2−} has the largest ionic radii (D) Mg^{2+} has the smallest ionic radii. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
sol: All have 10 electrons (A ✓); Z = 8, 9, 11, 12 (B ✗).

pyq.q: Choose the incorrect trend in the atomic radii (r) of the elements.
sol: Across a period radius falls: Mg 160 > Al 143, so "r_{Mg} < r_{Al}" is wrong.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I : The correct order in terms of atomic/ionic radii is Al > Mg > Mg^{2+} > Al^{3+}. Statement II : The correct order in terms of the magnitude of electron gain enthalpy is Cl > Br > S > O. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: Mg (160) > Al (143), so I fails at its first step.
|Δ_{eg}H|: Cl 349 > Br 325 > S 200 > O 141 → II true.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

pyq.q: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (A) Al^{3+} < Mg^{2+} < Na^{+} < F^{−} (B) B < C < O < N (C) B < Al < Mg < K (D) Si < P < S < Cl. List-II: (I) Ionisation Enthalpy (II) Metallic character (III) Electronegativity (IV) Ionic radii. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: A: isoelectronic ions → ionic radii (IV). B: B < C < O < N — the IE order with the N/O kink (I).
C: metallic character grows down/left (II). D: electronegativity across period 3 (III).

pyq.q: The incorrect decreasing order of atomic radii is
sol: Be (111) is SMALLER than Mg (160) — radius grows down a group.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement (I) : The radii of isoelectronic species increases in the order Mg^{2+} < Na^{+} < F^{−} < O^{2−}. Statement (II) : The magnitude of electron gain enthalpy of halogen decreases in the order Cl > F > Br > I. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

pyq.q: Given below are the two statements: one is labeled as Assertion (A) and the other is labeled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): There is a considerable increase in covalent radius from N to P. However from As to Bi only a small increase in covalent radius is observed. Reason (R): covalent and ionic radii in a particular oxidation state increases down the group. In the light of the above statement, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
sol: N 74 → P 110 (big jump); As 121 → Bi 148 (smaller steps) because filled d and f subshells shield poorly.
R is true, but it does not explain the SMALL increase — the d/f contraction does.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

pyq.q: A monoatomic anion (A^{−}) has 45 neutrons and 36 electrons. Atomic mass, group in the periodic table and physical state at room temperature of the element (A) respectively are
sol: A^{−} has 36 e^{−} → Z = 35 = bromine (group 17, a liquid).
Mass number = 35 + 45 = 80.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: K > Mg > Al > B is the correct order in terms of metallic character. Statement II: Atomic radius is always greater than the ionic radius for any element. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
sol: Metallic character: K > Mg > Al > B ✓ (down and to the left).
Anions are bigger than their atoms → II false.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

pyq.q: In period 4 of the periodic table, the elements with highest and lowest atomic radii are respectively.
sol: Across period 4 the radius falls: K (231) largest, Br (114) smallest (ignoring Kr).

pyq.q: Which of the following represents the correct trend for the mentioned property ? A. F > P > S > B - First Ionization Energy B. Cl > F > S > P - Electron Affinity C. K > Al > Mg > B - Metallic character D. K_{2}O > Na_{2}O > MgO > Al_{2}O_{3} - Basic character. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: D ✓ (oxides get more basic down and to the left).

pyq.q: Consider the elements N, P, O, S, Cl and F. The number of valence electrons present in the elements with most and least metallic character from the above list is respectively.
sol: Most metallic = least electronegative: P (5 valence electrons). Least metallic: F (7).

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement (I) : An element in the extreme left of the periodic table forms acidic oxides. Statement (II) : Acid is formed during the reaction between water and oxide of a reactive element present in the extreme right of the periodic table. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: Left (Na, K): basic oxides (Na_{2}O + H_{2}O → NaOH) → I false.
Right (Cl, S): acidic oxides (Cl_{2}O_{7} + H_{2}O → HClO_{4}) → II true.
o: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: The element that does not belong to the same period of the remaining elements (modern periodic table) is:
sol: Pd (Z = 46) is in period 5; Os (76), Ir (77), Pt (78) are in period 6.

pyq.q: Which of the following statements are NOT true about the periodic table? A. The properties of elements are function of atomic weights. B. The properties of elements are function of atomic numbers. C. Elements having similar outer electronic configurations are arranged in same period. D. An element's location reflects the quantum numbers of the last filled orbital. E. The number of elements in a period is same as the number of atomic orbitals available in energy level that is being filled.
sol: A ✗ (modern law uses atomic NUMBER). C ✗ (similar configurations make a GROUP). E ✗ (elements = 2 × orbitals).

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement (I) : The 4f and 5f-series of elements are placed separately in the Periodic table to preserve the principle of classification. Statement (II) : S-block elements can be found in pure form in nature. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
sol: f-block rows are placed below to keep elements with similar properties in one column → I true.
s-block metals are too reactive to occur free → II false.
o: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

pyq.q: If IUPAC name of an element is "Unununnium" then the element belongs to nth group of periodic table. The value of n is ____
sol: Z = 111 is Rg, below Cu, Ag, Au → group 11.
